author: Autodesk
description: Wrap deform a polygon mesh with moving points from an MPM Rubber simulation.
documentation:
## MPM Rubber

### What it does

This graph simulates a rubber material using the MPM Graph.

This graph demonstrates how to wrap deform a polygon mesh with moving points from a simulation. This example works in cases where there is a consistent point count and the points generally move together. If the simulation has points that break away, this will cause artifacts - like fracturing.

### Inputs and outputs

The inputs for this graph are the initial points of the objects and the procedurally modelled objects to be "rubberized".  The outputs utilize a `wrap_on_points` compound that conforms a polygon object for rendering to the MPM output points.  The final output is a mesh.

**Note:** for optimal results, including motion blur, it is recommended that this example be cached to disk before rendering.

### How it works

  - The `scatter_points` compound sets the initial positions for the two procedural objects.

  - The procedural objects (noughts and crosses) are then instanced to the points and baked to become the MPM source object.

  - The MPM simulation controls the behaviour of the objects.  The main settings for this are:
    * `mass_density` - how heavy the rubber is.  The larger this number, the more the rubber will push other objects around.

    * `volume_preservation` - how much the rubber will try to preserve it's shape. If this value is zero, it will not try to preserve any volume, if it is 1 it will behave like a liquid.  A setting of 0.5 is good for most simulations.

  - Once the simulation has been performed the points are sent to the `wrap_on_points` compound which will try to conform the mesh input to the points.  This compound has a radius (how far the point can move without distorting) input and a max number (how many points around each point to use for matching) input.
  - The weight input on `wrap_on_points` controls how closely the mesh conforms to the points.

_notes.text:
# Model the Objects

Modelling the O and the X for the simulation procedurally

# Set the inital positions

The ***scatter_points*** provides the initial positions to the MPM simulation, with the ***point_size*** allowing you to control the size of the final noughts and crosses

# Create and Bake Instances

Taking the positions from the ***scatter_points*** compound, the two geometries are instances on those points sequentially.

# Compute on Frame

This compound causes anything preceding it to only be computed on the frame specified.  This speeds up the graph by only doing the calculations once, on the frame specified.

# Wrap on Points

This is a wrap deformer compound that will wrap the original meshes to the simulated points.

_backdrops.title: Starting positions for Xs and Os

_notes.text: This gets all the face indicies of the object as an array.

When the *extrusion_path* port is empty, ***extrude_faces*** will use the face normal to perform the extrusion.

*divisions* allows you to set how the final extrusion is split up and *thickness* is the full length of the extrude.
This is an iterate loop that will perform an extrusion on the face indices set in the  ***indicies_to_extrude*** compound.
***indices_to_extrude*** is a quick and simple way of selecting which faces you wish to extrude on.  The face indices are entered as a comma separated string and returned as a long integer array.
This uses the current index of the loop to choose which face will be extruded.  The ***build_array*** compound is a single-value array provided to the ***extrude faces***.

When the *extrusion_path* port is empty, ***extrude_faces*** will use the face normal to perform the extrusion.

*divisions* allows you to set how the final extrusion is split up and *thickness* is the full length of the extrude.

The mesh output and input ports of the iteration loop have their *port_states* set.  This is telling the iterate loop to perform the contents of the loop on the last results of the loop, thereby ensuring that we have only one object on output, with different faces extruded.
This builds an accelerator structure to speed up sampling later in the graph.
Retrieves the *weight* property as set in the UI

in this section, the calculated transforms are converted to vectors and then the position is linearlly interpolated based on the weights.

Moves the points from "first" to "second" position based on the weight.

In this section, the points within a radius are sampled (using the accelerator setup outside the loop) and passed to the compound that computes the transforms for each point.

These transforms represent the best fit for moving the base points to the position of the target points.

_backdrops.title: Sample in radius and compute point transforms
